facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is that this cash is being returned to shareholders rather than held for creditors: first-half repurchases and dividends were 2.69x issuer-defined free cash flow, and the renewed buyback programme for the twelve months from 2026-07-02 allows purchases of up to a tenth of the public float. A second weakness is earnings quality: realized derivative losses of CAD 113.4 million in the first half came from oil contracts struck before the sale, and the issuer says no WTI hedges remain after the second quarter, so cash flow now follows the oil price directly. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C32

tables.limitation: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by shareholder distributions that exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026, because cash that supports creditors leaves the company, which implies a shrinking cushion if the pace continues. Countervailing evidence is a net cash position, creditor-first debt reduction and conventional governance. Ownership and legal capacity are not established, so the level rests on documented issuer behaviour.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Cash flow is the weak link because it moves with the oil price and no flat-price hedge remains after the second quarter. The operating netback rose from CAD 35.36 per boe in the first quarter of 2026 to CAD 55.33 per boe in the second as WTI rose from US$71.93 to US$92.79 per barrel, and issuer-defined free cash flow moved from CAD 1.7 million to CAD 128.0 million. Price, not volume, drove 82.24% of the second-quarter increase in sales net of blending against a year earlier. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Shareholder returns are the main channel through which the creditor cushion can leak, and the stated policy limits rather than removes that risk. Repurchases and dividends of CAD 349.1 million in the first half were 2.69x issuer-defined free cash flow, the renewed buyback programme allows purchases of up to a tenth of the public float until 2027-07-01, and the issuer targets a 15% annual total shareholder return. Against that, the issuer commits to keep a net cash position through 2028, seven of eight directors are independent and Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium. If the pace continued with free cash flow near nil, cash would last 12.17 months, which shows the size of the policy lever and not a forecast. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a less favourable view is that the second-quarter result reflects a price spike linked to the conflict in Iran, after the issuer records benchmark prices falling between the third quarter of 2024 and the fourth quarter of 2025 on OPEC+ and North American supply growth, and the pre-conflict price case gives about nil free cash flow while returns ran at 2.69x free cash flow in the first half. The view would weaken if the revolver were drawn to fund returns, if cash fell toward the CAD 89.2 million of notes, if the net cash commitment were withdrawn, if WTI stayed near or below the US$52 per barrel breakeven, or if the tax ruling went against the issuer. It would strengthen with audited statements and executed debt documents that confirm restricted-payment limits, and with a quarter in which free cash flow covers returns at a lower oil price. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Baytex is a Calgary-based oil and natural gas producer in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, with heavy oil assets at Peavine, Peace River and Lloydminster and light oil in the Viking and the Duvernay. Production was 71,243 boe/d in the second quarter of 2026, 88% oil and natural gas liquids, after the sale of the Eagle Ford assets for net proceeds of US$2.2 billion on 2025-12-19, which repaid most debt and left one small note. Revenue comes from selling crude at benchmark-linked prices with no contracted revenue stream disclosed, so cash flow is cyclical and price-driven, and customer concentration is not stated. The credit consequence is a business that can generate large cash flow in a strong market but offers no contractual visibility, which is why the balance sheet, not the business, carries the credit. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Baytex is a public company listed on the Toronto and New York exchanges with common shares carrying one vote each and no preferred shares; no controlling shareholder is named and holder percentages are not supplied. The group structure is simple in the documents, with indirect subsidiary entities holding the disputed tax losses, but guarantors, restricted groups and structurally senior debt are not listed. Funded debt is the US$64.1 million of 7.375% senior notes due 2032-03-15, issued 2024-04-01, and a CAD 750 million secured revolver maturing 2030-06-27 that is undrawn apart from CAD 4.4 million of letters of credit, so senior secured debt is CAD 4.4 million; the notes are redeemable from 2027-03-15 and at par from 2029-03-15. Behaviour rather than ownership therefore sets financial policy: the chief executive changed on 2026-05-07, two directors left and two were appointed on 2026-07-30, and Business & governance finds no creditor-adverse action and rates sponsor and governance risk medium. The credit consequence is that distributions, not sponsor extraction, are the risk to follow. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue follows volume and price, and price dominates: of the CAD 216.2 million increase in second-quarter sales net of blending against a year earlier, 82.24% came from price. Heavy oil is 74.29% of sales, so the WCS discount of US$14.62 per barrel, which widened from US$10.20 a year earlier, matters more than the WTI level alone, and egress to diversified markets is limited. No contract duration, pass-through or customer concentration is disclosed, and Baytex has no pricing power as a producer. Revenue is therefore cyclical and discretionary to the market, and the credit consequence is that earnings visibility is short while production growth of 11% gives some volume support. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Unit cash costs are stable while the netback moves with price: operating plus transport cost was CAD 17.28 per boe in the fourth quarter of 2025 and CAD 17.86 per boe in the second quarter of 2026, with operating cost per boe falling as volumes absorb fixed field costs. Royalties act as a partial stabiliser, at 13.01% of sales net of blending in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 16.0% in the second quarter of 2026, and blending and trucking costs rise with condensate prices and trucking rates. Margins can be defended against cost inflation only in part and not against a price fall, because unit costs do not fall when prices fall; a realized derivative loss of CAD 12.98 per boe, 23.46% of the second-quarter netback, shows how a hedge book set before the sale reduced the benefit of the price rise. facts.label: Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: first-half exploration and development spending of CAD 267.3 million used 75.70% of operating cash flow, and issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million was 31.99% of adjusted funds flow of CAD 405.6 million, with the first quarter near zero because spending then was CAD 145.0 million. Leasing and asset retirement settlements are small, and interest has turned from an expense to income as the debt was repaid. Claims outside the debt figure are lease obligations of CAD 60.3 million, transportation and processing commitments of CAD 70.9 million and asset retirement obligations of CAD 546.5 million, together CAD 677.7 million or 7.59x the carrying value of the notes, so fixed claims outside debt are larger than the debt itself even though they fall due slowly. The credit consequence is that free cash flow is available for debt service in any year in which price supports it, but conversion is price-dependent and the heavier second-half programme of CAD 357.7 million will test it. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry works through regional supply rather than share: Baytex is a price-taker, and the issuer says differentials fluctuate with production and inventory levels in Western Canada, with the widening of the heavy oil discount as the visible effect. New entrants matter little to credit because land, inventory and capital are the barriers, and the documents state 750,000 net acres of heavy oil and 91,500 net acres in the Duvernay. Substitutes appear only as a general risk factor on the effect of an energy transition on demand for petroleum products, with no quantified effect, and buyer power and customer concentration are not discussed, so neither can be assessed. Supplier power appears in rising trucking rates and condensate costs for blending. The credit consequence is a margin that depends on benchmark and logistics conditions that the issuer does not control. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The nine dimensions of the financial profile are assessed in sentences, each with a reason, and the table form of the scorecard is not written in this run. Scale and market position is average: production of 71,243 boe/d is meaningful but no peer data is supplied. Competitive advantage is average: inventory depth is long but the issuer is a price-taker. Business diversification is weak: one basin, 65% heavy oil and 50.06% of production from two areas. Cost and capex flexibility is average: spending is discretionary but sustaining capital is not disclosed. Margin stability is weak: the netback moved from CAD 35.36 to CAD 55.33 per boe in one quarter and reported EBITDA margin from 5.05% to 55.80%. Free cash flow stability is weak: issuer-defined free cash flow was CAD 1.7 million then CAD 128.0 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong: no maturity before 2030 and the notes trade at 103.45% of principal. Liquidity position is strong: cash and undrawn revolver of CAD 1,465.9 million against CAD 59.3 million of near-term obligations, with pro forma net debt of negative CAD 615.0 million after the dividend paid on 2026-07-02. Financial policy and governance is average: independent board and a net cash commitment, offset by distributions above free cash flow. The main supports are the balance sheet and liquidity, the constraints are price-geared cash flow and concentration, the trend is rising production with a heavier second-half programme, and the missing data are peers, reserves and the executed debt documents. Free cash flow stability is weak: issuer-defined free cash flow was CAD 1.7 million then CAD 128.0 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong: no maturity before 2030 and the notes trade at 103.45% of principal. Liquidity position is strong: cash and undrawn revolver of CAD 1,465.9 million against CAD 59.3 million of near-term obligations, with pro forma net debt of negative CAD 615.0 million after the dividend paid on 2026-07-02. Financial policy and governance is average: independent board and a net cash commitment, offset by distributions above free cash flow. The main supports are the balance sheet and liquidity, the constraints are price-geared cash flow and concentration, the trend is rising production with a heavier second-half programme, and the missing data are peers, reserves and the executed debt documents.

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to about 71,000 boe/d in 2026, a fourth-quarter exit rate near 72,000 boe/d and spending of about CAD 625 million, with a second Duvernay pad due in September, four more Duvernay wells in 2027 and up to two Utikuma exploration wells in early 2027; this supports volumes but loads capital into the second half, so free cash flow depends on a price above the fourth-quarter 2025 level of US$59.14 per barrel, at which the plan produces about nil free cash flow. Over three to five years management targets 6% to 8% annual production growth at a mid-cycle WTI price of US$70 per barrel while keeping net cash, a 15% annual total shareholder return and a possible Gemini final investment decision in 2027; the 2032 notes become callable at par from 2029-03-15, the revolver matures in 2030 and any tax judgment would arrive around 2028 to 2030, so refinancing and the tax matter fall within the period. Sector tailwinds are a strong benchmark price and tighter light crude markets; sector headwinds are the wider heavy oil discount, weak Canadian gas prices and rising trucking and condensate costs. Company tailwinds are Duvernay and Peavine well performance and the removal of interest expense; company headwinds are the absence of WTI hedges, the heavier capital plan and distribution pace. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a return of WTI from US$92.79 per barrel in the second quarter of 2026, a level the issuer links to supply disruption from the conflict in Iran, to the US$59.14 per barrel of the fourth quarter of 2025, after benchmark prices had fallen from the third quarter of 2024 to that quarter on OPEC+ and North American supply growth, with the heavy oil discount near US$14.62 per barrel. The first operational break is the netback, which would fall from CAD 55.33 to about CAD 29.30 per boe, the level of that quarter, which already reflects a lower royalty rate of 13.01%; no WTI hedge exists after the second quarter to offset the fall. Financial transmission is revenue and margin falling together: on guided volumes and the roughly CAD 625 million plan, annual free cash flow would be about negative CAD 12.1 million, so any returns would come from cash. The liquidity consequence is that returns at the first-half pace would use cash in about 12.17 months, but leverage and refinancing are unaffected in this period because the revolver of CAD 745.6 million is undrawn and no principal is due before 2030, and the tax claim would fall later. Management levers are stopping or slowing buybacks, which are discretionary under the programme, cutting capital spending, which was only CAD 267.3 million of the plan in the first half, and holding the dividend, which costs about CAD 16.1 million a quarter. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress inside 24 months, because the debt is small and the levers are in management's hands, and default risk is not supported by the evidence; what the scenario shows is that the cash cushion, not earnings, would absorb the price fall. The primary downside path is a lower oil price while buybacks continue at the first-half pace, with an adverse tax judgment as a later claim, and the observable trigger is returns above free cash flow while WTI trades near or below the US$52 per barrel breakeven. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Baytex presents an adequate business profile supported by growing production, long drilling inventory and discretionary capital, but credit quality is constrained by heavy oil and single-basin concentration, price-geared free cash flow and returns that exceeded free cash flow in the first half. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at second-quarter 2026 prices and weak at pre-conflict prices because the 2026 plan then produces about nil free cash flow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on management's choices rather than the market, because only the 2032 notes and an undrawn revolver to 2030 remain and the notes trade near 103.45% of principal. The primary downside path is a lower oil price while buybacks continue, consuming the cash cushion. Further analysis would require the audited 2025 statements, the executed credit agreement and indenture, reserves and sustaining capital data, and peer and rating inputs. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data is supplied. The financial profile trend is a falling cash balance as returns exceed free cash flow, with cash down CAD 234.6 million in the first half. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder returns running ahead of oil-price-dependent free cash flow. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied documents are enough for a credit snapshot of Baytex after the Eagle Ford sale, but only to the second quarter of 2026 and without audited annual statements or any executed debt document, so creditor protections stay unverified. The interim statements and second-quarter management discussion cover the balance sheet, the undrawn facility, the covenant positions and the one remaining senior note; guarantors, security, indenture terms, ratings and market prices are not established, and the annual information form is absent. The latest document is 98 days old at the cutoff, third-quarter 2026 results are not covered, and three printing differences in the issuer's own documents are logged, not resolved.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Baytex has almost no financial debt after the Eagle Ford sale, so creditors face negligible leverage; the risk to watch is cash leaving through shareholder returns, not debt service.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C03; calculation C06

At 2026-06-30 the one remaining note has a carrying value of CAD 89.2 million against cash of CAD 720.3 million, so net debt is negative CAD 631.1 million, meaning net cash. On the issuer's credit-agreement EBITDA, total debt is 0.12x and interest cover is 9.3x; reported twelve-month EBITDA cannot be built from the set. In six months, shareholder returns of CAD 349.1 million exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million and cash fell by CAD 234.6 million.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C16; calculation C22; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Leverage is negligible on every definition the sources allow. The only debt at carrying value is the CAD 89.2 million of notes due 2032, because the revolving facility was undrawn at 2026-06-30 and lease obligations of CAD 60.3 million are carried on their own lines. Cash of CAD 720.3 million therefore exceeds debt by CAD 631.1 million, against CAD 858.1 million at 2025-12-31 before the share repurchases and dividends of 2026. The issuer's own net cash figure is CAD 566.3 million because it also nets receivables, payables and inventory.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that this cash is being returned to shareholders rather than held for creditors: first-half repurchases and dividends were 2.69x issuer-defined free cash flow, and the renewed buyback programme for the twelve months from 2026-07-02 allows purchases of up to a tenth of the public float. A second weakness is earnings quality: realized derivative losses of CAD 113.4 million in the first half came from oil contracts struck before the sale, and the issuer says no WTI hedges remain after the second quarter, so cash flow now follows the oil price directly.

The view would change if cash fell toward the CAD 89.2 million of debt, if the revolver were drawn, or if the oil price fell back from the second-quarter average of US$92.79 per barrel; evidence of the audited 2025 statements or the credit-agreement EBITDA add-backs would also change how much weight the adjusted ratios can bear.

## Request

Business, ownership and governance fact pack for BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. (bte), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, issuer history and financial-policy behaviour as the seven supplied documents state them, with no peer ranking, instrument view or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Baytex has no sponsor or controlling owner stated in the documents, so governance risk to creditors rests on its own financial policy, which is to return cash to shareholders while keeping net cash, and nothing in the filings shows creditor-adverse action. Sponsor and governance risk is medium on documented behaviour.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; Source readiness (CP-0)

The business is a Western Canadian oil producer weighted to heavy oil, at 65% of production, so cash flow follows the oil price and the heavy-oil discount rather than a contracted income stream. First-half 2026 repurchases and dividends of CAD 349.1 million exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million, so the behaviour to monitor is the pace of distributions against cash created by the Eagle Ford sale. Ownership percentages, board control rights and the debt documents are not established.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C03
### Key findings

- No sponsor exists to assess, so conduct is read from the issuer's own actions. The documents describe a publicly traded company whose common shares carry one vote each and rank equally, with no preferred shares issued, and name no controlling shareholder; the holders and their percentages are not established because the annual information form is not supplied.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 10; 40-F_2025-12-31_bte-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2613640d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Creditor treatment has been favourable since the Eagle Ford sale. Net proceeds of US$2.2 billion closed on 2025-12-19 were followed by repayment of most of the credit facilities, redemption of the 8.5% senior notes and partial redemption of the 2032 notes, and the issuer later repurchased US$5.8 million of the 2032 notes at a premium to par.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-31_a991-2025yepressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 38; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 10

- The distribution policy is the behaviour to watch. First-half 2026 repurchases of CAD 316.3 million and dividends of CAD 32.8 million, together CAD 349.1 million, exceeded issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million, and the stated aim is a 15% annual total shareholder return from growth, dividends and buybacks. The issuer also says it will keep a net cash position through 2028, which is the commitment creditors can hold it to.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2613640d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_tm2613640d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03; calculation C04

- Governance looks conventional and stable. After the 2026-07-30 appointments seven of eight directors are independent, the chief executive succession was completed on 2026-05-07 with a new Chief Operating Officer, and the controls statements show no material weakness. Audit committee membership after one member stepped down is not stated.

- Heavy oil drives the operating model. Heavy oil was 65% of Q2 2026 production and 74.29% of petroleum and natural gas sales before blending costs, and the issuer buys diluent and relies on trucking and pipelines, so realised prices depend on the heavy-oil discount, diluent cost and transport cost. No WTI hedges remain after Q2 2026.

- The structure is simple but not fully mapped. The set names one wholly-owned subsidiary, a former U.S. credit facility borrower, and describes indirect subsidiary entities that hold the tax losses disputed with the tax authority, but it lists no guarantors, restricted group or collateral.

- Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for creditors. Quarterly statements, management discussion and covenant levels are published, while the executed debt documents, the annual information form and the audited annual statements are not in the set, and the second-quarter release carries two printing differences.

Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_bte-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 40-F_2025-12-31_bte-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 7; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that creditor protection rests on a policy rather than on any document in the set. No indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so the restricted-payment and debt-incurrence limits that the notes summary calls standard cannot be read, and leverage could rise if buybacks or the Gemini thermal project, which may reach a final investment decision in 2027, were funded with borrowing.

The view would change if the revolver were drawn to fund distributions, if the net cash commitment were withdrawn, or if an annual information form disclosed a shareholder with control or consent rights; steady quarterly reporting, no covenant waiver or exchange offer in the set, and cash that exceeds debt many times over would argue for keeping the current view.
### Limitations

- The annual information form is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling shareholder exists rests on silence in the interim documents; a disclosed holder with board or consent rights would turn it into a governance risk.

- The indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so capacity to pay distributions is judged from cash on hand alone; a tight restricted-payment test would make distribution risk legal as well as behavioural.

- Related-party transactions and management fees are not disclosed in any interim document, so the absence of value leakage is not confirmed; any such payments would move the sponsor and governance risk level from medium toward high.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The set describes one transformative transaction, the sale of the Eagle Ford business, which closed on 2025-12-19 for net proceeds of US$2.2 billion. Proceeds were used first to repay most of the credit facilities and redeem the 8.5% senior notes and part of the 2032 senior notes, and later to fund share repurchases; a separate fifteen-year take-or-pay agreement with Gibson Energy was converted into a lease obligation in February 2026.

No new debt issue is stated in the documents for 2025 or 2026: the senior notes outstanding were issued on 2024-04-01, the facilities were reduced and extended rather than increased, and the only debt movement in 2026 is a small repurchase of those notes. The date and terms of the facility amendment are not stated.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Baytex is well covered for creditors today because it holds net cash and an undrawn revolver, but its cash flow follows the oil price without flat-price hedges, so creditors rely on management keeping shareholder returns within free cash flow. At 2026-06-30 net debt was negative CAD 631.1 million, or negative CAD 615.0 million pro forma after the CAD 16.1 million dividend paid on 2026-07-02, against CAD 745.6 million of undrawn revolving capacity.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

In the first half of 2026 repurchases and dividends of CAD 349.1 million were 2.69x issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million, and cash fell by CAD 234.6 million. At the oil price of the fourth quarter of 2025 the 2026 plan produces roughly no free cash flow, so a price fall would be met from the cash cushion, not from earnings. The business profile is adequate and the balance sheet is strong; the primary downside path is a lower oil price while buybacks continue.

### Key findings

- The balance sheet leaves creditors with no near-term repayment or refinancing pressure. The only debt is the 2032 senior notes, with a carrying value of CAD 89.2 million, against cash of CAD 720.3 million, so net debt is negative CAD 631.1 million, or negative CAD 615.0 million pro forma after the CAD 16.1 million dividend paid on 2026-07-02; July repurchases are not reflected because their cost is not stated. The secured revolver is undrawn, with CAD 745.6 million available until 2030-06-27, and liquidity of CAD 1,465.9 million is 24.73x the CAD 59.3 million of contractual obligations due within a year.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash flow is the weak link because it moves with the oil price and no flat-price hedge remains after the second quarter. The operating netback rose from CAD 35.36 per boe in the first quarter of 2026 to CAD 55.33 per boe in the second as WTI rose from US$71.93 to US$92.79 per barrel, and issuer-defined free cash flow moved from CAD 1.7 million to CAD 128.0 million. Heavy oil is 74.29% of sales and 65% of production, so the heavy oil discount of US$14.62 per barrel also reaches cash flow, and 42.07% of heavy oil volumes carry a basis hedge that fixes that discount only to the end of 2026. Price, not volume, drove 82.24% of the second-quarter increase in sales net of blending against a year earlier.

- At pre-conflict prices the 2026 plan absorbs almost all cash flow, so distributions would draw on cash. The management sustaining breakeven of US$52 per barrel leaves a cushion of only US$7.14 at the fourth-quarter 2025 price. - Shareholder returns are the main channel through which the creditor cushion can leak, and the stated policy limits rather than removes that risk. Repurchases and dividends of CAD 349.1 million in the first half were 2.69x issuer-defined free cash flow, the renewed buyback programme allows purchases of up to a tenth of the public float until 2027-07-01, and the issuer targets a 15% annual total shareholder return. Against that, the issuer commits to keep a net cash position through 2028, seven of eight directors are independent and Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium. If the pace continued with free cash flow near nil, cash would last 12.17 months, which shows the size of the policy lever and not a forecast.

- Capital spending is discretionary, which is the main protection if prices fall, but the second half is heavier than the first. Exploration and development spending was CAD 267.3 million in the first half, 75.70% of operating cash flow, against a plan of about CAD 625 million, so CAD 357.7 million is implied for the second half, 33.86% above the first. Management raised production guidance while holding spending, and 58 net wells of the year's heavy oil programme, more than half, are due on stream in the second half, so free cash flow at constant prices should be lower than in the first half.

- The business is concentrated in one basin and one commodity group even though inventory is long. Heavy oil is 65% of production, Peavine and Lloydminster together are 50.06% of production, and every producing area is in Western Canada, so a regional price or egress problem would reach most cash flow at once. Management cites about 12 years of heavy oil drilling inventory and a deep Duvernay inventory, which supports durability only as far as management's statements can be tested, because reserves and sustaining capital are not supplied.

- Debt structure and market access are simple and favourable. Only US$64.1 million of the 2032 notes remain, callable from 2027-03-15 and at par from 2029-03-15, with a fair value of 103.45% of principal at 2026-06-30, and the revolver matures on 2030-06-27. The covenants are far from binding: interest cover is 9.3x against a 3.5x minimum and total debt is 0.1x Bank EBITDA against a 4.0x maximum, and the notes carry no significant financial maintenance covenants. Refinancing depends on the issuer's choices, not on market windows.

- A tax dispute is the largest contingent claim on cash, but it is not a near-term payment. The tax authority asserts CAD 493.1 million of tax, late payment interest and penalty for 2011 to 2015, against insurance cover of CAD 272.5 million; no payment is required during the appeal, and the issuer expects about two years for a Tax Court judgment and possibly two more for further appeals. The amount ultimately owed depends on the liable entity and unused tax shelter, so the asserted figure is a ceiling for scale and not an estimate of loss.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is the size of the cushion: cash is 8.07x the carrying value of debt, interest cover is 9.3x, net interest has moved from an expense of CAD 41.5 million in the second quarter of 2025 to income, and management controls both capital spending and buybacks within the year. On that evidence a default within 24 months would need a prolonged oil price collapse, buybacks continuing regardless and an adverse tax ruling together, and the evidence does not support assuming that combination.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_a991-q22026fs.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 38; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 44; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-08-05_tm2619297d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C05; calculation C31; calculation C30

The strongest evidence for a less favourable view is that the second-quarter result reflects a price spike linked to the conflict in Iran, after the issuer records benchmark prices falling between the third quarter of 2024 and the fourth quarter of 2025 on OPEC+ and North American supply growth, and the pre-conflict price case gives about nil free cash flow while returns ran at 2.69x free cash flow in the first half. The view would weaken if the revolver were drawn to fund returns, if cash fell toward the CAD 89.2 million of notes, if the net cash commitment were withdrawn, if WTI stayed near or below the US$52 per barrel breakeven, or if the tax ruling went against the issuer. It would strengthen with audited statements and executed debt documents that confirm restricted-payment limits, and with a quarter in which free cash flow covers returns at a lower oil price.

- No peer set, rating or market price is supplied, so scale, diversification and cost position are judged against the issuer's own record and its management's statements, and any peer data showing a materially larger or less concentrated producer would raise the business assessment above adequate.

- The price cross-check holds one observed quarter's netback, guided volume and the first-half overhead constant for a year, so the near-nil free cash flow at the fourth-quarter 2025 price is an illustration whose size would move with royalty, differential and capital choices; it supports the direction of the downside path, not its amount.

- The liable taxpayer, unused tax shelter and the insurance policy terms are not stated, so the cash effect of the tax dispute is bounded only by the asserted amounts and the insurance cover; the downside scenario treats it as a later claim, and an earlier judgment would bring it forward.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is the net cash balance sheet: debt of CAD 89.2 million against cash of CAD 720.3 million and an undrawn revolver removes debt service as a source of stress, so any deterioration would have to come through cash returned to shareholders, not through lenders. The pro forma net debt after the dividend paid on 2026-07-02 is negative CAD 615.0 million.

The second strength is a long and simple debt profile: only the 2032 notes and a revolver maturing 2030-06-27, covenant positions far from their limits and a note fair value of 103.45% of principal mean refinancing is a choice rather than a need.

### Company description

Baytex is a Calgary-based oil and natural gas producer in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, with heavy oil assets at Peavine, Peace River and Lloydminster and light oil in the Viking and the Duvernay. Production was 71,243 boe/d in the second quarter of 2026, 88% oil and natural gas liquids, after the sale of the Eagle Ford assets for net proceeds of US$2.2 billion on 2025-12-19, which repaid most debt and left one small note. Revenue comes from selling crude at benchmark-linked prices with no contracted revenue stream disclosed, so cash flow is cyclical and price-driven, and customer concentration is not stated. The credit consequence is a business that can generate large cash flow in a strong market but offers no contractual visibility, which is why the balance sheet, not the business, carries the credit.

### Ownership and group structure

Baytex is a public company listed on the Toronto and New York exchanges with common shares carrying one vote each and no preferred shares; no controlling shareholder is named and holder percentages are not supplied. The group structure is simple in the documents, with indirect subsidiary entities holding the disputed tax losses, but guarantors, restricted groups and structurally senior debt are not listed. Funded debt is the US$64.1 million of 7.375% senior notes due 2032-03-15, issued 2024-04-01, and a CAD 750 million secured revolver maturing 2030-06-27 that is undrawn apart from CAD 4.4 million of letters of credit, so senior secured debt is CAD 4.4 million; the notes are redeemable from 2027-03-15 and at par from 2029-03-15. Behaviour rather than ownership therefore sets financial policy: the chief executive changed on 2026-05-07, two directors left and two were appointed on 2026-07-30, and Business & governance finds no creditor-adverse action and rates sponsor and governance risk medium. The credit consequence is that distributions, not sponsor extraction, are the risk to follow.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue follows volume and price, and price dominates: of the CAD 216.2 million increase in second-quarter sales net of blending against a year earlier, 82.24% came from price. Heavy oil is 74.29% of sales, so the WCS discount of US$14.62 per barrel, which widened from US$10.20 a year earlier, matters more than the WTI level alone, and egress to diversified markets is limited. No contract duration, pass-through or customer concentration is disclosed, and Baytex has no pricing power as a producer. Revenue is therefore cyclical and discretionary to the market, and the credit consequence is that earnings visibility is short while production growth of 11% gives some volume support.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Unit cash costs are stable while the netback moves with price: operating plus transport cost was CAD 17.28 per boe in the fourth quarter of 2025 and CAD 17.86 per boe in the second quarter of 2026, with operating cost per boe falling as volumes absorb fixed field costs. Royalties act as a partial stabiliser, at 13.01% of sales net of blending in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 16.0% in the second quarter of 2026, and blending and trucking costs rise with condensate prices and trucking rates. Margins can be defended against cost inflation only in part and not against a price fall, because unit costs do not fall when prices fall; a realized derivative loss of CAD 12.98 per boe, 23.46% of the second-quarter netback, shows how a hedge book set before the sale reduced the benefit of the price rise.

### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: first-half exploration and development spending of CAD 267.3 million used 75.70% of operating cash flow, and issuer-defined free cash flow of CAD 129.8 million was 31.99% of adjusted funds flow of CAD 405.6 million, with the first quarter near zero because spending then was CAD 145.0 million. Leasing and asset retirement settlements are small, and interest has turned from an expense to income as the debt was repaid. Claims outside the debt figure are lease obligations of CAD 60.3 million, transportation and processing commitments of CAD 70.9 million and asset retirement obligations of CAD 546.5 million, together CAD 677.7 million or 7.59x the carrying value of the notes, so fixed claims outside debt are larger than the debt itself even though they fall due slowly. The credit consequence is that free cash flow is available for debt service in any year in which price supports it, but conversion is price-dependent and the heavier second-half programme of CAD 357.7 million will test it.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry works through regional supply rather than share: Baytex is a price-taker, and the issuer says differentials fluctuate with production and inventory levels in Western Canada, with the widening of the heavy oil discount as the visible effect. New entrants matter little to credit because land, inventory and capital are the barriers, and the documents state 750,000 net acres of heavy oil and 91,500 net acres in the Duvernay. Substitutes appear only as a general risk factor on the effect of an energy transition on demand for petroleum products, with no quantified effect, and buyer power and customer concentration are not discussed, so neither can be assessed. Supplier power appears in rising trucking rates and condensate costs for blending. The credit consequence is a margin that depends on benchmark and logistics conditions that the issuer does not control.
### PEST factors

Political and economic factors are material and social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. The issuer attributes the oil price rise since March 2026 to the conflict in Iran and related supply disruptions, which makes the second-quarter price a policy and geopolitical outcome that can reverse, and royalties rise with price. Climate and energy transition rules appear only in the general risk factors with no quantified effect, so they do not change the 12 to 24 month view. Currency matters because the 2032 notes are in U.S. dollars while the issuer reports in Canadian dollars; the credit effect is small today because the notes are small against cash.
### SWOT
- Strengths: net cash with an undrawn revolver, a simple debt stack and rising production support creditors by removing near-term refinancing and debt service pressure.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The nine dimensions of the financial profile are assessed in sentences, each with a reason, and the table form of the scorecard is not written in this run. Scale and market position is average: production of 71,243 boe/d is meaningful but no peer data is supplied. Competitive advantage is average: inventory depth is long but the issuer is a price-taker. Business diversification is weak: one basin, 65% heavy oil and 50.06% of production from two areas. Cost and capex flexibility is average: spending is discretionary but sustaining capital is not disclosed. Margin stability is weak: the netback moved from CAD 35.36 to CAD 55.33 per boe in one quarter and reported EBITDA margin from 5.05% to 55.80%. Free cash flow stability is weak: issuer-defined free cash flow was CAD 1.7 million then CAD 128.0 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong: no maturity before 2030 and the notes trade at 103.45% of principal. Liquidity position is strong: cash and undrawn revolver of CAD 1,465.9 million against CAD 59.3 million of near-term obligations, with pro forma net debt of negative CAD 615.0 million after the dividend paid on 2026-07-02. Financial policy and governance is average: independent board and a net cash commitment, offset by distributions above free cash flow. The main supports are the balance sheet and liquidity, the constraints are price-geared cash flow and concentration, the trend is rising production with a heavier second-half programme, and the missing data are peers, reserves and the executed debt documents.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to about 71,000 boe/d in 2026, a fourth-quarter exit rate near 72,000 boe/d and spending of about CAD 625 million, with a second Duvernay pad due in September, four more Duvernay wells in 2027 and up to two Utikuma exploration wells in early 2027; this supports volumes but loads capital into the second half, so free cash flow depends on a price above the fourth-quarter 2025 level of US$59.14 per barrel, at which the plan produces about nil free cash flow. Over three to five years management targets 6% to 8% annual production growth at a mid-cycle WTI price of US$70 per barrel while keeping net cash, a 15% annual total shareholder return and a possible Gemini final investment decision in 2027; the 2032 notes become callable at par from 2029-03-15, the revolver matures in 2030 and any tax judgment would arrive around 2028 to 2030, so refinancing and the tax matter fall within the period. Sector tailwinds are a strong benchmark price and tighter light crude markets; sector headwinds are the wider heavy oil discount, weak Canadian gas prices and rising trucking and condensate costs. Company tailwinds are Duvernay and Peavine well performance and the removal of interest expense; company headwinds are the absence of WTI hedges, the heavier capital plan and distribution pace.
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a return of WTI from US$92.79 per barrel in the second quarter of 2026, a level the issuer links to supply disruption from the conflict in Iran, to the US$59.14 per barrel of the fourth quarter of 2025, after benchmark prices had fallen from the third quarter of 2024 to that quarter on OPEC+ and North American supply growth, with the heavy oil discount near US$14.62 per barrel. The first operational break is the netback, which would fall from CAD 55.33 to about CAD 29.30 per boe, the level of that quarter, which already reflects a lower royalty rate of 13.01%; no WTI hedge exists after the second quarter to offset the fall. Financial transmission is revenue and margin falling together: on guided volumes and the roughly CAD 625 million plan, annual free cash flow would be about negative CAD 12.1 million, so any returns would come from cash. The liquidity consequence is that returns at the first-half pace would use cash in about 12.17 months, but leverage and refinancing are unaffected in this period because the revolver of CAD 745.6 million is undrawn and no principal is due before 2030, and the tax claim would fall later. Management levers are stopping or slowing buybacks, which are discretionary under the programme, cutting capital spending, which was only CAD 267.3 million of the plan in the first half, and holding the dividend, which costs about CAD 16.1 million a quarter. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress inside 24 months, because the debt is small and the levers are in management's hands, and default risk is not supported by the evidence; what the scenario shows is that the cash cushion, not earnings, would absorb the price fall. The primary downside path is a lower oil price while buybacks continue at the first-half pace, with an adverse tax judgment as a later claim, and the observable trigger is returns above free cash flow while WTI trades near or below the US$52 per barrel breakeven.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Baytex presents an adequate business profile supported by growing production, long drilling inventory and discretionary capital, but credit quality is constrained by heavy oil and single-basin concentration, price-geared free cash flow and returns that exceeded free cash flow in the first half. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at second-quarter 2026 prices and weak at pre-conflict prices because the 2026 plan then produces about nil free cash flow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on management's choices rather than the market, because only the 2032 notes and an undrawn revolver to 2030 remain and the notes trade near 103.45% of principal. The primary downside path is a lower oil price while buybacks continue, consuming the cash cushion. Further analysis would require the audited 2025 statements, the executed credit agreement and indenture, reserves and sustaining capital data, and peer and rating inputs. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data is supplied. The financial profile trend is a falling cash balance as returns exceed free cash flow, with cash down CAD 234.6 million in the first half. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder returns running ahead of oil-price-dependent free cash flow.
